source_pipeline: configs/countries/us.yaml → sync_socrata.py + sync_census_popest.py → raw.us_sf_employee_comp → dbt_us_staging (+ seeds seed_us_sf_job_family_display / seed_us_sf_job_reclass) → dbt_us_intermediate → dbt_us_analytics → dbt_us_marts → export_us_sf_payroll.py
fiscal_year_note: SF fiscal year N runs July 1 (N-1) to June 30 N. All figures are FISCAL-year accounting only — the source publishes every row under BOTH Calendar and Fiscal accountings and mixing them double-counts (the dataset's #1 trap).
attribution_note: A person paid under several job codes in a year is counted ONCE, under the family that paid them the most, and their whole annual compensation is attributed to it — so these counts add up to the citywide headcount exactly. This is NOT the same measure as n_employees in payroll_by_family_year.json, which counts a dual-role person in both families (that file splits dollars, this one splits people).
ladder_note: p25/p50/p75 are exact percentiles of per-person annual total compensation (salary + overtime + other pay + benefits) inside each family. A family's median reflects how much of the year its people are paid for as much as its hourly rates: the families the City staffs seasonally sit low on the ladder.
histogram_note: Buckets of $25,000 from $0; the top bucket is open (ceiling_usd null). Named cells under 5 people are pooled into the count-only 'Other roles' row of the same year, which names no family. Zero-count buckets are omitted. Summed over families, these cells reproduce the citywide histogram in payroll_distribution.json exactly.

privacy.rule: No dollar aggregate in this file covers fewer than 5 employees. Groups under 5 people are pooled into visible 'Other roles' rows per department; pools that would themselves stay under the threshold are folded into the department total with no row. Departments under the threshold (the Law Library in practice, 2-3 people) are included in citywide totals but not listed.
privacy.measured_cost: Pooling moves ~1.2% of total dollars into visible 'Other roles' rows; the department-level fold is under $600k/year (<0.01% of compensation). Nothing is removed from totals.
privacy.count_only_disclosures: Counts of employees above fixed thresholds (>$200k…>$500k) are published exactly, including values under 5: they attach no dollar amount to any group. The source itself is public at row level (pseudonymized); this site publishes aggregates only.
